query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH recommendations page presents a Table A that organizes recommended protective clothing barriers into explicit "8 hr" and "4 hr" groups (example rows show entries labeled "8 hr: ..." and "4 hr: ..."). [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The provided archived NIOSH excerpt in the evidence inventory does not include a visible row for hydrogen chloride (the HCl-specific 8‑hour and 4‑hour barrier assignments are not present in the supplied archive excerpt). [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The New Jersey Hazardous Substance Fact Sheet for hydrogen chloride states: 'Hydrogen Chloride is a CORROSIVE CHEMICAL and contact can severely irritate and burn the skin and eyes.' [Hazardous Substance Fact Sheet: https://nj.gov/health/eoh/rtkweb/documents/fs/1012.pdf]
- The New Jersey fact sheet further states: 'Contact with liquid Hydrogen Chloride may cause frostbite.' [Hazardous Substance Fact Sheet: https://nj.gov/health/eoh/rtkweb/documents/fs/1012.pdf]
- The New Jersey fact sheet states inhalation effects: 'Hydrogen Chloride can affect you when inhaled' and that higher exposures can cause lung injury and delayed pulmonary edema; it also lists workplace exposure limits: OSHA PEL 5 ppm (ceiling), NIOSH REL 5 ppm (not to be exceeded at any time), and ACGIH TLV 2 ppm (ceiling). [Hazardous Substance Fact Sheet: https://nj.gov/health/eoh/rtkweb/documents/fs/1012.pdf]
